newsitem.title: USA: Anadarko sees rising oil production.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko sees rising oil production.

text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp expects oil production from its core fields to rise steadily and will direct cash flow into a portfolio of exploration prospects in the coming years, executives said on Tuesday.

The company on Monday announced it and partners were awarded three North Atlantic tranches in the United Kingdom's 17th bid round. The partners expect to begin drilling on their brightest prospect, tranche 61 northwest of the Shetland Islands, next year, the Anadarko executives said.
"The mapped structures we have seen have the possibility to be giant, I mean giant, oil fields," Anadarko Chairman Robert Allison said.
Anadarko this year has drilled two of ten wildcat wells in its Algeria leaseholdings, and remains undeterred after the initial wells proved non-commercial, he said.

The company also plans to begin drilling in Eritea after acquiring 4,500 kilometers of seismic data last year and will drill a pair of stratigraphic wells under a basalt layer in Jordan's Safawi Block to test possible formations there, he said.

Overall, the company has spudded 105 wells onshore so far this year and will easily eclipse the 206 wells spudded in all of last year. "One of Anadarko's strengths is the depth of our portfolio," he said.
Production in 1997 is expected to increase to 44 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe) this year and rise steadily to 76 mmboe in the year 2000, up from 38 mmboe production in 1996, he said.
